title: The Pull Request Review Workflow
intro: Reviewing a teammate's pull request well means actually running it, checking CI, and merging cleanly — all doable from the terminal.

steps.fake_output:
#51  feat: saved carts           feature/saved-carts  about 2 hours ago
#49  chore: bump eslint to v9     deps/eslint9         about 1 day ago
steps.why: A quick daily look keeps reviews from piling up — slow reviews are one of the biggest drags on delivery speed.

steps.prompt: Check out PR #51 locally to test it yourself.
steps.explanation: The PR's branch is fetched and checked out.
steps.why: Reading a diff shows what changed; running the code shows whether it works. For anything non-trivial, actually running it catches things review alone misses.

steps.prompt: Check the status of the CI checks on PR #51.
steps.fake_output:
build   pass  1m10s
test    pass  2m44s
lint    pass  22s
deploy-preview  pass  3m01s  https://pr-51.preview.acme.dev
steps.explanation: All checks green, plus a preview environment URL.
steps.why: Branch protection should REQUIRE these checks before merging — relying on people to remember to look is how broken code reaches main.

steps.prompt: Approve the PR with a comment.
steps.why: Saying how you reviewed ('tested locally') helps the author and future readers understand how thoroughly it was checked.

steps.prompt: Squash-merge it and delete the branch.
steps.fake_output:
✓ Squashed and merged pull request #51 (feat: saved carts)
✓ Deleted branch feature/saved-carts
steps.explanation: The PR's commits become one commit on main, titled after the PR.
steps.why: Squash merging keeps main's history to one commit per change — which makes 'git revert' of a whole feature a single clean operation during an incident.
